scope: PR5 ask-dismiss copy: full fresh audit of all 10 ui.chat.asks keys for fr, read side by side with en and the en context. Requested head 5b10cb570 had moved to 9571f33c5 by audit time; `git diff 5b10cb570 9571f33c5 -- src/i18n i18n` is empty, so the audited bytes are those of both heads. Cross-surface comparison against harness tui.asks/relay.ask at 93f798ddb (lo-stale-ask-surfaces, unmerged branch). No rendered-fit claim.

findings.issue: The note addresses the operator with a second-person imperative (vous-imperative « n’attendez plus »), so it reads as telling the operator to stop waiting for a reply. Per the context sidecar the actor is the agent: dismissing means the agent stops waiting on this ask. The terminal/phone copy for the same English (tui.asks.dismiss.moot_note, relay.ask.dismiss.moot_note) was corrected for exactly this in its own independent audit and names the agent. Root cause is upstream of the translation: the en context sets `tone: "lowercase fragment, imperative"` for this key while its `note` says the agent stops waiting, so a translator following the tone line lands on an operator-addressed imperative. Coder should also change that tone line (e.g. 'lowercase fragment naming what the agent stops doing') so a re-translation does not regress.

Two defects. (1) The many arm renders {count} while one/other render #, so 1 000 000 renders as the unformatted '1000000 de messages' (verified with the repo's intl-messageformat); the fr style guide says '# renders the formatted number'. (2) « message de vous » is a calque of 'from you'; « de votre part » is the idiomatic French. Reachable only at exact multiples of 10⁶ messages, so user impact is negligible; graded MINOR because it breaks a style-guide rule.

findings.issue: Verb diverges from the terminal/phone surfaces for the same act (« Ignorer cette question », « ignorer… », « Ignorée — … »); the heading's own context says these are 'the same words the terminal and phone surfaces use'. Applies to dismiss.heading, dismiss.trigger, dismiss.receipt.moot and dismiss.receipt.answered_in_chat. The noun « demande » is kept (see fr-n1).

findings.issue: Cross-surface divergence: the terminal/phone heading uses « question » for the ask, the desktop uses « demande ». Kept deliberately: « demande » matches the desktop's own asks panel and rail on the same screen (ui.chat.composer.secret_ask_open « Ouvrir les demandes », ui.shell.rail.ask.aria « Demandes »). Recorded so the two surfaces can converge in one direction; no catalogue change proposed here.
